Class Paginator

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.jpa.spring.page.Paginator
public final class Paginator extends Object
Converts framework-agnostic PageSpec requests into Spring Data Pageables, and Spring Data Pages back into framework-agnostic PageDtos.

A paginator is configured once, for one entity type and sort enum, and reused. It is immutable and thread-safe, so the usual home for one is a static final constant in the service that pages:

private static final Paginator PAGINATOR = Paginator.of(Person.class, PersonSort.class, cfg -> cfg
        .defaultSort(PersonSort.LAST_NAME)
        .defaultPageSize(25));

public PageDto<PersonDto> search(String term, PageSpec spec) {
    return PAGINATOR.paginate(spec, pageable -> repository.search(term, pageable), PersonDto::of);
}

Stable ordering

SQL only orders rows whose sort values differ; rows that tie may come back in any order, and each page is a separate query, so tied rows can repeat on one page and vanish from another. To prevent that, every Pageable ends with a tiebreaker: one or more unique properties, sorted ascending, appended after the requested sort (and used alone when nothing else is sorted). The default tiebreaker is "id", the identifier of BaseEntity. Entities whose unique property is named differently configure it with Paginator.Config.tiebreaker(String...); Paginator.Config.noTiebreaker() opts out.

Property validation

When a paginator is built, every sort enum constant's property and every tiebreaker property is checked against the entity type, using the same property-path rules Spring Data applies at query time. A typo or a missing property therefore fails when the paginator is created (typically at class initialization or in the first test), not as a PropertyReferenceException on every request. Queries that sort by something other than entity properties, such as native queries sorting by column names, opt out with Paginator.Config.skipPropertyValidation().

Sort resolution

  1. PageSpec.sortBy() given: the matching enum constant, or UnknownSortByValueException if none matches. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; matching is case-sensitive.
  2. sortBy absent or blank, and a default sort configured: the default.
  3. Otherwise only the tiebreaker (or unsorted, when the tiebreaker is disabled).

The requested PageSpec.sortDirection() applies to the sort property (ascending when absent); the tiebreaker is always ascending.

Paging defaults

  • Missing or negative page index: 0
  • Missing page size: the configured default (20 unless changed)
  • Requested page sizes are clamped to 1..maximum (100 unless changed)
  • A null spec is treated as a spec with every value missing

    • of

      public static <S extends Enum<S> & SortPropertyProvider> Paginator of(Class<?> entityType, Class<S> sortEnumClass, Consumer<Paginator.Config<S>> customizer)
      Creates a paginator for the given entity type and sort enum, customizing the default settings. 
      Paginator.of(MemberDirectoryEntry.class, MemberSort.class, cfg -> cfg
        .tiebreaker("identityId")
        .defaultSort(MemberSort.NAME)
        .defaultPageSize(25)
        .maxPageSize(100));
      Type Parameters:
      S - the sort enum type
      Parameters:
      entityType - the entity the paged queries return; sort and tiebreaker properties are validated against it unless Paginator.Config.skipPropertyValidation() is set
      sortEnumClass - the enum whose constant names are the accepted sortBy values
      customizer - adjusts the settings
      Returns:
      the paginator
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the resulting settings are inconsistent, or a sort or tiebreaker property is not a property of entityType
